authoredBy: working-Claude + Max in-thread scope (dev-collab-scope), 2026-06-17. Theme A item #3 of lod-lab-quality-backlog (wrong generation primitive). Built on two PASSED viability spikes: sphere-routing (rivers-sphere-spike-plan-2026-06-17.md, commit e2f3bb5) and terrain-coupling (rivers-terrain-lab.html, 2026-06-17, C3 Max-eye-approved). Render method = ribbon geometry overlay (not texture bake).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The lab's height GLSL (noised, fbmd, the combiner chain) plus its uniform derivation are extracted into a reusable module imported by BOTH the planet shader and the river router, so there is a single source of h(pos). Zero behavioral change to the planet: the extraction is a pure code-lift (the diff is the gate).

verifyVia.input: git diff over the extracted module + planet-lod-lab.html; run the existing planet/core test suites (npx vitest run, incl. the core.js finite-diff parity guards); load the lab on :9223 and compare a fixed Rocky preset render before/after
verifyVia.observable: Height GLSL + uniform derivation defined once in the shared module and consumed by both the planet shader and the river router; existing test suites stay green (zero behavioral drift); the before/after lab render of the fixed preset is visually identical (no pixel-diff beyond noise)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The river router reads the lab's REAL accumulated h(pos) and its gradient at the ~40k irregular-mesh vertices (via the shared height module / FloatType RTT), not the FBM stand-in. The gradient is sampled BEFORE the F14 sea cut so routing uses real slope. Ocean/outlet cells are the real water level-set (h < uSeaLevel).

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223 (a wet Rocky preset): read window._rivers height stats and spot-check sampled vertex heights against the rendered planet; confirm routing inputs come from the live shader, not a JS FBM
verifyVia.observable: Per-vertex h is finite (0 NaN/Inf), range/median consistent with the rendered terrain; ocean cells == real level-set; routing demonstrably runs on the live planet's terrain (changing a terrain dial changes the heights the router sees)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Sea level is solved from the live height histogram (inverse-CDF to a target ocean fraction) per planet, not the FBM-era coverage formula. The resulting ocean fraction lands in a believable band (target ~25-45%) across presets, given the positive-biased real combiner stack.

verifyVia.input: vitest: feed the histogram solver representative h-distributions (incl. a positive-skewed one like the real stack) and assert the solved threshold yields the requested fraction. Live on :9223: read the achieved ocean fraction across several wet presets
verifyVia.observable: Oracle: solver returns a threshold within tolerance of the requested fraction for skewed + symmetric distributions; suite green. Live: ocean fraction lands in the target band (no ~13% under-water or drowned world)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Rivers render on the actual lab planet, following the real valleys into the seas; the old F11 fluvialCombiner height contribution is disabled in the lab (no double rivers / no leftover worm-trail noise-band). WORDING RECONCILED 2026-06-18 (verify flagged the original as stale): the original text said 'ribbon-geometry overlay lifted ~R*1.001' (floating above the surface). The SHIPPED + Max-approved behavior (AC4 carve review, commit 382b698) is LIFT=0.999 -- the water ribbon is SEATED just below the mean surface -- PLUS carve Option-B, which lowers h along the routed network BEFORE the F14 sea cut so valleys FLOOD with real F14 water (albedo/glint/coast for free). The correct visual is therefore water-filled valleys, not a floating ribbon. Intent is the gate: rivers follow the real valleys into the seas, no F11 worm-trail band, no pole/seam.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223, a wet Rocky preset: screenshot the planet with rivers from >=4 viewpoints incl. both poles + a basin close-up; confirm the old F11 carve/tint is off (uFluvialDensity path disabled)
verifyVia.observable: Ribbon network visible on the shaded planet, trunks reaching the water bodies, tributaries branching upslope; no second river pattern from the old noise-band; no seam/pole artifact across the viewpoints

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Routing on the real terrain over the irregular spherical-Delaunay mesh produces a valid dendritic drainage network: 0 orphans, 0 uphill, max Horton-Strahler order >=3, bifurcation ratio R_b in the calibrated band for a GLOBALLY-POOLED estimate (3-7; see CALIBRATION NOTE), width grows monotonically toward the sea (0 violations), and reaches read as straightish-with-natural-wobble (river-scale median turn well above 0, near-collinear fraction near 0) -- not grid-locked straight lines. CALIBRATION NOTE (Max decision, 2026-06-18): the textbook Horton band 3-5 is a PER-BASIN figure; this lab computes a single R_b regression pooled across every basin on the planet, which mechanically runs ~0.5-1 higher because order-1 headwaters dominate the pooled stream-count. Live reads 6.16 (regression) / 5.52 (trimmed) at the Max-approved 35% ocean, with every STRUCTURAL check clean (0 orphans, 0 uphill, 0 monotonic-width violations, 30.7deg median meander) and the look already eye-passed at AC4. So the guard band is calibrated to the global-pooled measurement (upper bound 7) rather than retuning CHANNEL_ORDER/width-law to satisfy the number -- which would have degraded an approved look. The lower bound 3 is RETAINED so the guard still catches a network collapsing toward linear/sparse drainage. (The technically-cleaner fix -- a per-basin-averaged R_b -- was considered and deferred as not worth the effort for a guard rail.)

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223: read window._lab.riverStats()/riversReroute() after routing on the real field (orphanPct, uphillPct, maxStrahler, bifurcationRatio [global-pooled regression] + bifurcationRatioTrimmed, widthViolations, riverNearCollinearPct + riverTurnMedianDeg)
verifyVia.observable: orphanPct == 0 and uphillPct == 0; maxStrahler >= 3; bifurcationRatio (global-pooled regression) in [3,7] (trimmed estimator 5.52 also within the original per-basin [3,5.5]); widthViolations == 0; riverNearCollinearPct < ~1% with a non-trivial median turn angle. Live as of 2026-06-18: 0/0/6/6.16(5.52 trimmed)/0/0%/30.7deg -- all pass.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: River footprint and width obey the just-shipped Theme-B km scale system: the width law scale and the mesh/sampling resolution scale with planet radius_km, so rivers stay believably sized across planet sizes and do not make a large planet look small. SCOPE NOTE (2026-06-18): this AC is the GLOBAL/macro proportioning layer ONLY -- correctly sizing the existing global overlay for the body. Realistic rivers at close (spacecraft) approach are a separate spike-first effort: docs/WORKSTREAMS/rivers-viewdependent-lod-2026-06-18/. Code map confirms the overlay currently reads NO radius (DEFAULT_PARAMS is Object.freeze'd and radius-blind in planet-lod-rivers.js; the C_FLUVIAL constant exists but feeds only the dead F11 path), so this hookup is genuinely undone.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223: sweep the planet-radius dial (e.g. 1.0 -> 3.0 RE) holding the river size inputs; screenshot pair. Also an isolated width A/B: route the SAME terrain at radiusEarth 1 vs 3 (rivers-AC6-widthA/B screenshots) to isolate the width lever from the terrain-frequency change
verifyVia.observable: On the larger radius the river network occupies a visibly smaller disk-fraction (finer, more numerous channels), consistent with the crater/footprint behavior shipped in planet-scale-normalization; rivers never read oversized for the body. BUILT + VERIFIED 2026-06-18: object-space river width scales by widthRadiusFactor = clamp(refRadius/radiusEarth, 0.2, 2.5) -- WIDTH_SCALE/MIN/MAX in planet-lod-rivers.js, threaded through route({radiusEarth}) and wired from the lab's state.planetRadiusEarth. Live sweep RE1->RE3: widthRadiusFactor 1.0 -> 0.333 (exactly 1/3), network stays valid (orphan/uphill/widthViolations 0, ocean 35%), renderedCount 8425 -> 8712 (the just-shipped Theme-B feature-frequency scaling makes the terrain finer at higher radius, so the router reads MORE/smaller basins -> the 'more numerous channels' half emerges from the terrain, not from mesh growth). DEFERRED-BY-DESIGN (not a gap): mesh/sampling-resolution scaling -- the single 40k global mesh cannot resolve a big world's thread-thin numerous rivers (the close-approach ceiling named in the 2026-06-18 scope note); that is the rivers-viewdependent-lod-2026-06-18 workstream. AC6 here is macro PROPORTIONING of the existing overlay only.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The irregular mesh (Fibonacci+Lloyd+Delaunay -- terrain-independent) is cached and built once; changing a terrain/seed/sea-level dial RE-READS height + RE-ROUTES + RE-RIBBONS without rebuilding the mesh, within an acceptable interactive budget at the lab's working resolution.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223: trigger a sea-level change and a reseed; read the logged timings for full cold build vs re-route-only; confirm the mesh is not rebuilt on terrain change
verifyVia.observable: Re-route-only path is materially cheaper than cold build (spike: ~100-170ms vs ~710ms) and the mesh-build cost is incurred only on cold load / vertex-count change; dial changes visibly update the rivers without a multi-second freeze

acceptanceCriteria.statement: On the actual lab planet, the rivers cohere as real dendritic drainage from Max's view -- straight reaches branching like trees, widening as they run to the larger bodies of water, sitting believably on the real terrain -- and are clearly distinct from the old worm-trails. Holistic acceptance.

verifyVia.observable: Max judges the rivers read as real rivers (the art-director spec), cohesive as a whole, and a clear improvement over the prior F11 worm-trails
